run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-259 had issues on November 20, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: Only Loki answered in this Run; every Kubernetes, Prometheus and Jaeger call returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so the assessment rests on payment-api's own log lines. In namespace app-259, pod payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 (stream labels job=payment-api, service=payment-api) logged 8 ERROR lines with the exact message "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted" between 2026-11-20T13:46:00Z and 14:44:00Z; a query covering the whole authorized window returned only those 8 lines (13:46, 13:54, 14:03, 14:15, 14:19, 14:21, 14:31, 14:44), so in the sampled data the deviation begins at 13:46 UTC, just after the reported 13:45, and the observed error burst ends at 14:44. Every error line carries wait_time_ms 1227-4840 and queue_length 5-15, i.e. requests waited seconds for a connection while up to 15 were queued. Successful payment INFO lines continue interleaved (13:42, 13:59, 14:49) and the sampled INFO cadence during the incident resembles the rest of the day, so the pod kept serving; the error rate cannot be quantified without metrics. What exhausted the pool (a slow or unavailable database dependency, or an undersized pool-size configuration on the workload) is not observable with the available sources, so no root-cause object is named and the conclusion is partial.

claims.text: Pod payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 in namespace app-259 (labels job=payment-api, service=payment-api, level=ERROR) logged the exact line "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted" at 2026-11-20T13:46:00Z, 13:54:00Z, 14:03:00Z, 14:15:00Z, 14:19:00Z, 14:21:00Z, 14:31:00Z and 14:44:00Z.

The pool-exhausted query covered the whole authorized window (2026-11-20T03:49:17Z to 2026-11-21T03:49:17Z), returned 8 lines with truncated=false, and reports source_start_at 2026-11-20T13:46:00Z and source_end_at 2026-11-20T14:44:00Z.

A 1-minute count_over_time of the same filter over 2026-11-20T12:00:00Z-16:00:00Z shows single-line events at 13:46:36, 13:54:12, 14:03:42, 14:15:06, 14:19:51, 14:21:45, 14:31:15 and 14:44:33, with no such line counted earlier in that window.

The error payloads carry wait_time_ms and queue_length pairs of 1227/10, 2104/11, 1495/8, 2965/9, 4005/10, 4840/8, 2358/15 and 3836/5, so acquisitions waited 1.2-4.8 seconds with 5-15 requests queued.

A 10-minute sum by (namespace, pod_name, level) (count_over_time) series for this pod over 2026-11-20T12:00:00Z-18:00:00Z shows level=ERROR counts of 1-3 per step persisting from 13:46 through roughly 14:53, alongside INFO steps of 1-2, so the error stream was continuous rather than a single spike.
The same pod kept logging INFO "Payment processed successfully" at 13:42:00Z, 13:59:00Z and 14:49:00Z, inside and after the error span.

A cluster-wide Loki filter {namespace!=""} |~ "(?i)error|fail|exhaust|timeout|refused|panic" over 2026-11-20T13:00:00Z-14:30:00Z returned exactly one stream, payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 (6 error lines, all pool-exhausted); no other namespace or pod appears in that returned result.

Over 2026-11-20T03:49:17Z-20:00:00Z the query {namespace!=""} returned 26 lines from exactly two streams, the INFO and ERROR streams of payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12, earliest 04:24:00Z; the only messages present in the returned lines are "Payment processed successfully" and the pool-exhausted error.

Sampled success volume, sum(count_over_time({namespace="app-259"} |= "Payment processed successfully" [30m])) evaluated over 2026-11-20T04:31:30Z-2026-11-21T03:41:45Z, stays at about 1-3 lines per 30-minute step all day, including 1-2 per step in the 13:44-14:28 span around the incident.

The observed mechanism is saturation of the database connection pool used by payment-api, producing acquisition waits of up to 4.8 s with queues of up to 15 and then failures; the evidence does not show whether saturation came from a slow or unavailable database dependency or from an undersized pool-size setting on the workload.

A configuration object belonging to the payment-api workload, for example a ConfigMap holding a connection-pool limit or a fault-injection setting in effect at 13:45, could explain the saturation, but no ConfigMap, Deployment or pod template was read because the Kubernetes API was unavailable, so no Kubernetes object is named as the cause.

A total outage of payment-api is not supported: successful payment lines appear at 13:59:00Z and 14:49:00Z and the sampled INFO volume during the incident matches the day's baseline, so the pod was serving some requests while pool errors occurred.

A restart or crash-loop of payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 is not supported by its logs: across 2026-11-20T04:24:00Z-19:25:00Z the 26 returned lines contain no startup, boot, listening or crash messages, only INFO success and ERROR pool-exhausted lines; restart counts themselves could not be read because Kubernetes was unavailable.

gaps: Kubernetes was unavailable for every call (kubernetes_jq_query for pods and events, kubernetes_tabular_query for pods, fetch_pod_logs all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so pod phase, restart count, container lastState/exit code, Deployment-to-ReplicaSet-to-Pod ownership, events and ConfigMaps are unknown; whether the pod restarted or had a pool-size setting applied around 13:45 cannot be checked.

Prometheus was unavailable (execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names, get_prometheus_target returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so traces_span_metrics_calls_total error rates and latency for service payment, rpc client and server duration series, and kube-state-metrics were never consulted; those signals are unknown, not zero.

Jaeger was unavailable (traces_list_services, traces_search_by_tags returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no spans, error spans or parent references exist in this evidence and no call edge between payment-api and its database or its callers can be inferred.

The database dependency implied by the pool-exhausted message is never named in the logs and no logs from it were retrieved; Loki returned only the two payment-api streams, so other services' application logs were not available to check.

Two Loki views returned status no_data: 7cb94fe4-1db0-4f6c-9280-72d755b01fab-t1:5e1bc374-c438-4dba-9b82-f35a13078b54 (query excluding the payment-api pod, window 2026-11-20T13:00:00Z-14:30:00Z) and a11d2df2-6431-4f45-ba3c-0655c6775328-t0:6ad2e743-726f-4ff1-9359-57462fabf125 (query {namespace="app-259"} excluding success and pool-exhausted lines, full window); these show only that those queries matched nothing and cannot establish absence of other log content.

Loki timestamps are ingest/parse times and the returned lines are sparse (~1-3 per 30 minutes), so the exact onset and recovery of the degradation are bounded only by the observed error lines; the error rate and total failed-payment count are not observable from this log sample.
Change history is not integrated in this Run, so no deployment, rollout or configuration change around 13:45 UTC could be reviewed.
next_steps: Retry the Kubernetes API to read pod payment-api-259-d8f7b9c4-abc12 status, container lastState and exit code, restart count, its ReplicaSet/Deployment owners, and events in namespace app-259 for 13:30-15:00 UTC.
Read the payment-api Deployment and its ConfigMaps for connection-pool settings (pool size, max connections, acquire timeout) or fault-injection flags in effect near 13:45 UTC.

Restore Prometheus access and check payment error and latency series (traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment"} broken out by status code, rpc client duration) plus the database dependency's own saturation metrics, to determine whether the pool exhaustion originated downstream.
Check Services, Endpoints and NetworkPolicies for the database used by payment-api to rule out connection refusal as an additional cause.
